ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the practical filing of beneficial-owner information; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing procedures; Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of each UBO, general partner and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public registry or notary in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuer (utility provider or bank) together with local notary authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing and register extract of any corporate shareholder or corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant foreign companies registry or trade register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or power of attorney authorizing the incorporation of the Luxembourg SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, notary or competent corporate body in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for the underlying family assets
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supporting private bank or financial institution, notarily certified where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors and authorized signatories against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, OFAC SDN lists (for USD payment rails), and Luxembourg domestic sanctions and FATF high-risk jurisdiction references. Domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates, automatically trigger enhanced due diligence requiring senior-management approval and, where necessary, a report to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). Negative screening against a minimum of two independent commercial databases is required. Any unresolved sanction, PEP or adverse-media hit results in mandatory refusal of the engagement. Ongoing monitoring and transaction screening must continue after formation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online filing via MyGuichet.lu (https://www.lbr.lu and https://www.myguichet.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp may adopt a name in any language provided it is written in Latin (Roman) script and includes the mandatory statutory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. Names must be distinguishable from existing corporate names, must not be misleading, and must comply with French/German/Luxembourgish linguistic norms where required by the registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may request a renewal of the name reservation once for a further 30-day period through LBR before expiry, subject to continued availability. If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a reasoned objection or reconsideration request through MyGuichet.lu within 15 days of the refusal notification. After a final administrative refusal, the applicant may file an appeal with the competent Luxembourg administrative or commercial court within three months of notification. As an alternative, the applicant may immediately submit an amended or entirely new name application. Legal counsel should pre-clear any name containing sensitive tokens with the Minister of Justice or the relevant sectoral authority before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for RCS registration purposes, provided a Luxembourg registered agent accepts service of process and the registered office is a real identifiable address in Luxembourg. For this single-family-office investment holding structure, however, a pure virtual office will not satisfy banking AML due diligence or OECD substance expectations. The SCSp must have a local managing partner or authorized local agent, local records, evidence of board-level investment decisions, and a physical presence reasonably accessible for on-site inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. The estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 10% in the first financial year and approximately 5% per year thereafter for a compliant SCSp with a local registered agent. The risk increases to approximately 25% if a virtual office is used, if material management functions are outsourced outside Luxembourg, or if any UBO has a residence in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Law on Commercial Companies of 10 August 1915), as amended, Articles 102-1 to 102-13 (SCSp special limited partnership regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 implementing AIFMD), supplemented by the Law of 12 July 2013 on Alternative Investment Fund Managers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société / Acte de société (Partnership Agreement / Articles of Association), executed either as a notarial deed (acte notarié) or a private deed (acte sous seing privé) and filed electronically with the RCS via the LBR e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; no escrow or blocked-account requirement. The partnership agreement freely determines capital and contributions; prudent practice reserves a nominal working capital (e.g., EUR 1,000), and the private bank may require a funding comfort letter for account opening.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the initial general partner hereby approves and adopts the partnership agreement constituting the Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale (SCSp) named ______, with its registered office (siège social) at ______, Luxembourg.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial general partner subscribes to and accepts the partnership interests and contributions as set out in the agreement, and that the limited partners' subscriptions are recorded in the partnership accounts.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as gérant of the SCSp, acting alone, with full authority to represent the partnership in all dealings.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the gérant is authorized to file the partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, to arrange publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations, and to open a bank account in the name of the SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — e-name portal / RCS front desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative search in the RCS database to confirm the intended corporate name (e.g., 'FAMILY HOLDING SCSp') is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing registrations; optionally reserve the name for 30 days. The SCSp name must include 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'.
required_dossiers: Name request form signed by the proposed general partner
Extract of criminal record (casier judiciaire) of the individual general partner, or certificate of good standing of a corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness grounds, submit two or three alternative names; a second search is free of charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if real estate contribution or notarial form preferred); otherwise directly by the signatory partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles including corporate object (holding of financial assets for a single family), duration, identity of the general partner with unlimited liability, limited partners with capped liability, contribution and distribution clauses, and representation powers. Execute the agreement by all partners; use notarial form when the contribution includes immovable Luxembourg property.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Passport or national ID of each partner
If a corporate general partner: memorandum and articles, RCS extract, board resolution appointing a representative
Proof of residential address of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later flags the object clause as overly broad, amend the articles to restrict the object to private asset holding and family wealth administration and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBR e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed partnership agreement in PDF/A format together with the electronic application, attach the consent letter of each legal representative and his/her identity document, pay the EUR 30 registration fee, and obtain the RCS registration number and extract.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (PDF/A)
Electronically signed legal representative consent form (formulaire F)
Copy of identity card/passport of each legal representative
Proof of payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for further information (complément d'information), file a curative addendum within 15 days; the first correction is free of charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration entry for publication in RESA within one business day after registration; verify online that the published data match the executed partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: No separate filing required — automatic publication by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact LBR support citing the RCS number; factual errors in publication are corrected by a formal request to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the E-103 business start-up declaration with the ACD and AED via the myGuichet.lu portal; obtain the identification number (numéro d'identification) and, if applicable, the VAT number. Register for communal business tax with the administration of the commune of the registered office.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (certificat de non-radiation)
Executed partnership agreement
Identity documents of the representatives
Lease agreement or deed evidencing the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax number is not attributed within ten days, file a late-registration claim supported by the RCS extract; late attributions are backdated to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) — Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, complete the electronic RBE declaration identifying the direct or indirect beneficial owners, namely the general partner and any limited partner ultimately holding more than 25% of interests or control; for a family office structure, attach the ownership chart.
required_dossiers: RBE electronic declaration form
Identification documents of each ultimate beneficial owner
Ownership and control chart of the family arrangement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct a defective RBE statement by filing an amending statement; statutory fines apply for omission, so prompt rectification with the RBE service is essential.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private bank (professional client acceptance); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Luxembourg private-banking current or custody account in the SCSp's name with the gérant's mandate and the bank's KYC documents; if staff will be employed, register the employer with CCSS and file the DPAE preliminary declaration for each employee.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Executed partnership agreement
Legal representation mandate signed by the gérant
If employees: DPAE pre-employment declaration and CCSS employer registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking KYC is refused, provide a legal opinion on the family office structure and source of wealth, and, in case of disproportionate de-risking, file a complaint with the CSSF; CCSS late registrations are cured by subsequent filing with possible penalty mitigation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale de l'industrie et des services; no industrial or economic licence is required for an own-assets single family office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — a single family office investing only the founding family's assets is not a licensed financial sector professional under the Law of 5 April 1993; no CSSF licence and no registration as a Professional of the Financial Sector (PSF) is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Department of Environment, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-only administrative use; no full EIA report and no environmental registration required under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental assessments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the municipal wastewater ordinance (règlement communal) for sanitary sewage; no volatile organic compound (VOC) or industrial emission sources; office waste handled by municipal collection services under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the commune's occupation authorization and fire safety certificate under municipal building regulations; complete workplace clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under Articles L. 312-1 et seq. of the Labour Code, including emergency exits, first-aid equipment, and annual workplace risk assessment in accordance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 July 2006.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; online portals: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SCSp, the general partner or a Luxembourg-resident approved statutory representative must first file the partnership's incorporation deed and amendments with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS). Upon RCS registration, the ACD automatically assigns a national taxpayer identification number (matricule). The AEDT allocates a separate Luxembourg VAT identification number upon filing VAT registration form (Formulaire 640/645) through MyGuichet.lu. Non-resident partners do not require a Luxembourg tax ID solely for holding partnership interests, but the SCSp must provide the beneficial owner declarations under the RBE register and maintain a Luxembourg registered address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a general US-style check-the-box system. An SCSp is statutorily tax transparent by default and, as a general rule, is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax; its partners are taxed directly on their allocated share of income. Targeted elective alignment measures are available under the Luxembourg hybrid-mismatch rules implementing EU ATAD, allowing a taxpayer to file an election with the ACD to align Luxembourg characterization with a foreign jurisdiction's characterization in order to eliminate double non-taxation or double deduction outcomes. Where contrary classification is proven, the tax authorities may require a binding ruling before recognizing transparency for treaty purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for non-established foreign taxable persons; every taxable supply of goods or services in Luxembourg requires VAT registration from the first transaction. EU distance sales of goods threshold is EUR 10,000 annual across all EU Member States. Luxembourg-established small undertakings are exempt below EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover, but this exemption is not generally available to foreign entities making Luxembourg supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no domestic real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping for B2B e-invoices. E-invoicing is permitted where authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability are guaranteed, typically through EDI, PEPPOL, or qualified electronic signatures. E-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to Luxembourg public-sector entities using the Factur-X or UBL format. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu. No SAF-T filing obligation is in force for ordinary taxpayer groups. Luxembourg is actively monitoring the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposal, which may introduce real-time transaction reporting in future years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier obtains and retains documentary proof of export within the statutory time limit (normally by the end of the following month, with extension possibilities up to 90 days). Zero-rating also applies to certain intra-Community dispatches to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State, subject to the customer's valid VAT ID and inclusion in the recapitulative statement. Services supplied by an SCSp that is acting as a taxable person and whose place of supply is outside Luxembourg (e.g., services to non-EU business counterparties under the general B2B 'place-of-business' rule) are treated as zero-rated for Luxembourg VAT purposes, provided the supplier obtains sufficient documentary evidence of the non-resident status and business use of the recipient. Investment management and family-office advisory services provided to non-EU clients may fall under resource-of-service exceptions; a detailed written analysis and holding of contemporaneous evidence is required in every case.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT authorities, through the AEDT, conduct targeted post-export audits and cross-checks with customs records. If zero-rating is claimed without valid export proof, the tax may be clawed back retroactively with VAT under-declaration interest at the statutory rate (currently 9% per annum or such rate as adjusted by the Luxembourg Parliament) and an administrative fine. Intentional or repeated fraudulent zero-rating, including false invoicing, false customs declarations, or sham export document fabrication, incurs penal surcharges of up to 200% of the VAT evaded, criminal fines, and imprisonment for responsible officers under Articles 150 et seq. of the Luxembourg VAT Law. In addition, the AEDT may impose joint liability on the supplier, the customs agent, and the managing partner and may re-open closed assessments for ten years in cases of tax fraud or use of abusive arrangements. The inward remittance certificate, banking flows, bill of lading, and customs export declaration must be consistent; any inconsistency is treated as prima facie evidence of simulated export and triggers full clawback with penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and under European Central Bank (ECB) oversight; foreign exchange regulatory and statistical-reporting functions are shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital and current-account convertibility under the euro-area framework and EU Treaty freedoms (TFEU Articles 63-66). There are no exchange-control restrictions, prior authorisation requirements, surrender duties, or repatriation ceilings for resident or non-resident investors. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, partnership distributions, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred within the EU/EEA and converted into any currency at commercial bank rates without BCL or CSSF approval. The only practical constraints are bank-level AML/KYC documentary requirements; no statutory convertibility rationing applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion obligation. For an SCSp investment-holding entity, all euro and foreign-currency receipts may be retained in the original currency, remitted offshore, or converted freely at market rates. The BCL SHSS statistical reporting regime applies only to direct cross-border flows exceeding EUR 12,500 per calendar month or 50 transactions per year, and is purely statistical, carrying no conversion consequence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Private banking operational account in EUR/USD; capital escrow sub-account; securities custody
Operational multi-currency account; TARGET2-Securities (T2S) custody clearing; capital escrow account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Domestic operational and escrow accounts; dedicated SEPA clearing rail
Family-office private banking account; multi-currency treasury; securities custody; capital escrow
Wealth structuring and custody account; private banking current account; FX treasury line
Cross-border multi-currency client account; investments and custody; capital escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (CSSF passport under PSD2) and EEA EMIs can technically provide SEPA and limited SWIFT capabilities, but family-office-grade structuring, securities custody, deposits at central banks, and sophisticated FX execution require a full credit institution. UK EMIs lost EU passporting post-Brexit and would require CSSF licensing or an EEA branch. EMIs cannot hold client securities, cannot offer MiFID investment services, and their safeguarding obligations do not provide deposit-guarantee protection; therefore they are unsuitable for SCSp capital deposits or investment clearing, and may serve only as pre-funding gateway accounts with enhanced governance constraints.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law imposes no statutory in-person appearance requirement for directors; however, CSSF AML/CFT circulars (12/2017, 18/698) and bank internal policies require positive identification of the general partner(s) and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs with >25% interest or control). For foreign-owned SCSp family offices, tier-1 private banks de facto require an in-person or secure video-conference AML interview with directors, UBOs, and the authorised signatory, supported by certified passport copies, proof of residential address, tax identification numbers, notarised partnership deeds, and register extracts. Remote onboarding via CSSF-compliant e-KYC video identification is feasible for simpler structures, but enhanced due-diligence mandates above EUR 1 million typically mandate a physical or video interview with a banker and compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity of the SCSp partnership structure: fully private, no mandatory beneficial-ownership register filing for a non-regulated SCSp, and no statutory publication of accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société), SCSp capital-interest ledger, signed UBO declaration aligned with CSSF register form, AML organisational chart, notarised attestation or TRAK legal opinion identifying every natural-person UBO, and a written confirmation that the SCSp is used exclusively as a single-family passive investment vehicle, with the family governance charter annexed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity for multigenerational or inherited family assets with incomplete documentary provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: At least 24 months of pre-existing bank statements from the family's primary wealth manager, audited family-office consolidated accounts, inheritance or succession tax declarations, notarial deeds of donation or settlement, gift-tax filings, UBO's prior personal tax returns, and a forward-looking liquidity/asset-flow statement reconciling the initial contribution to documented accumulated wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border concentration and intermediary-layer sensitivity: the SFO controls underlying entities in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart with jurisdiction rationale, OECD/EU defensive-measures status confirmation, per-entity CRS/FATCA self-certifications, independent sanctions/PEP negative-hit reports from a reputable compliance data provider, commercial rationale memorandum for each intermediary layer prepared by counsel, and evidence of economic substance of underlying operating entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-sector concentrated asset position: family office holding one large illiquid operating asset, creating valuation and fraud-exposure concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent valuation report prepared by a Big-Four or recognised third-party valuer, audited financial statements of the underlying operating group for the last three fiscal years, medium-term liquidity budget showing the family office's cash-flow buffer, and a signed treasury and risk policy demonstrating diversification intentions and concentration limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed foreign tax identification number or missing CRS / FATCA self-certification for UBOs and the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete CRS and FATCA self-certification forms in the OECD/XSD format, tax residence certificates issued by competent tax authorities of each UBO, signed reliance letter addressed to the bank covering the SCSp and its direct owners, and a written representation that all TINs and birth-date metadata are accurate, with penal consequences acknowledged.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro-area contributors: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer directly to the SCSp's segregated EUR operational/escrow account; no FX purpose code is required intra-EEA, but the reference field must identify the partnership and the capital contribution and, for amounts above EUR 12,500 or 50 transactions annually, the BCL SHSS statistical purpose code for 'investment holdings / direct investment contributions' must be reported. For non-EEA flows (e.g., Switzerland, United Kingdom, Asia, GCC): SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg beneficiary bank, showing the SCSp as beneficiary, the family trust or foundation as remitter, IMF/BPM6-compatible purpose code for 'direct investment equity contribution' (ECB BoP classification code 5001/5002), and a free-format description: 'Equity contribution to Luxembourg SCSp investment holding vehicle (ISIC 6430)'. Verification requires documented source of funds, signed investment mandate, UBO attestation, execution of the bank's CDD file, and, where the contribution exceeds the bank's internal large-exposure notification threshold, an optional advance notice. No exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are selected by counterparty jurisdiction and instrument type: (i) intra-EEA obligations and fee payments: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit; (ii) non-EUR global disbursements and investment subscriptions: SWIFT MT103/MT202 cover payments with repayment purpose codes matching the underlying equity, loan, or capital-call instrument; (iii) private-equity capital-call funding: irrevocable transaction-matched SWIFT MT103 or standby/commercial letter of credit issued by the Luxembourg settling bank on behalf of the SCSp; (iv) physical-trade instruments where the family office holds operating assets: documentary and standby letters of credit under UCP 600 and URDG 758, with bill-of-lading verification by the negotiating bank; (v) securities settlement and custody-related cash movements: TARGET2-Securities (T2S) euro settlement via the custody bank, with same-day FX executed via SWIFT MT300 confirmation for non-euro trades. All outbound payments are matched against underlying contract value dates to eliminate daylight overdrafts and FX settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX fixed-date and window forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP, and liquid EMEA/APAC crosses) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA;
Currency-option strategies: vanilla European-style FX options with upfront premium, bought zero-cost collars, and risk-reversal structures for downside protection on unrealised investment exposures;

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies (offshore CNH, BRL, INR, RUB) where physical settlement is prohibited or impractical, executed with a bank counterparty under ISDA definitions;
FX swaps (swap-outright combinations) for short-term liquidity alignment across value dates without creating a notional credit facility;

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for long-term structural alignment of EUR-based family-office financing against USD or other-currency investment portfolios, including mark-to-market and collateral posting via CSDs;
Currency-index swaps and payment-currency-swapped equity derivatives limited strictly to risk-management purposes, recorded at fair value through the family office's treasury ledger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SCSp, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal reminder, administrative daily penalties, court-imposed fines, and may ultimately result in administrative strike-off from the RCS and personal manager liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership information (UBO/RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Ultimate Beneficial Owner register (RBE) at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 September for calendar-year entities; for non-calendar filing references, within the statutory annual RBE confirmation cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely or false UBO declarations expose the SCSp and its managers to administrative fines, criminal fines (up to EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases), and deregistration proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit when two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total EUR 6,250,000; net turnover EUR 12,500,000; average workforce 50 employees. Subsidiaries or entities operating under CSSF-regulatory regimes (e.g., SIF/SICAR) must always be audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Luxembourg law of 10 August 2015; the Luxembourg legal form of an SCSp applies the same accounting and reporting framework. IFRS optional for unlisted entities but required for public-interest entities if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year, an SCSp must reconfirm or update the RBE record by 30 September. Even unchanged structures must file the annual confirmation; any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must additionally be declared within one month of the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (members) with contributions and transfers
Minutes and written resolutions of partners/general partner
Register of corporate documents and contracts (agreements and administrative files)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office, corporate agent and routine filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 20,000 for a typical SCSp statutory audit; USD 10,000 - USD 40,000 if the SCSp falls under CSSF fund regulation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City composite rate: 17.00% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal rates vary between approximately 20.85% and 27.04%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Luxembourg SCSp is by default fiscally transparent and is thus not subject to corporate income tax at entity level; profits are allocated to partners. For taxable Luxembourg corporate partners, the effective aggregate CIT rate is relieved by the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (Article 166 LIR), the 80% IP box exclusion (Article 50bis LIR), and EU anti-fragmentation rules. No statutory tax holidays apply to family-office SCSp structures, but an SFO SCSp may be structured so that non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment are not subject to Luxembourg income tax on passive investment income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Schedule Form 200F (Transfer Pricing and Related-Party Transactions) filed through the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) electronic filing system (eCDF / e-Tax / professional e-filing portal). A transparent SCSp is not itself a Form 200 filer unless it has corporate features or it is operated through a taxable arrangement; resident partners carrying on a Luxembourg taxable activity via the SCSp must report their allocable share on their own tax returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly instalments of corporate income tax are due for taxable corporate residents. Dividend withholding tax declarations and VAT returns follow their own separate quarterly/monthly calendars.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a corporate taxpayer with a tax year ending 31 December, the income tax return is statutorily due by 31 March of the following year. Where the return is filed electronically through a registered Luxembourg tax adviser, the ACD grants an automatic extension to 30 September of the following year. Further extensions may be granted on reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, RCS number, Luxembourg fiscal number (matricule), legal form, registered office, general partner/managing director and tax representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner should reference the SCSp's Luxembourg RCS and fiscal identifiers in any counterparty withholding or tax-residence forms; if the partner has a Luxembourg permanent establishment, the partner's own return must identify the PE and the SCSp allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, profit and loss account, profit allocation, net worth, and deferred tax items as prepared under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp no partnership-level return is filed; the financial items are analytically attributed to partners in proportion to their capital/p&l sharing ratios, subject to the de minimis tests for a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / taxable result and tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income, participation exemption, IP box, interest limitation, loss carry-forward use, tax credits and final tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners report only Luxembourg-source income attributable to the SCSp activity; passive capital gains are generally not taxable in the absence of a Luxembourg PE or real property exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of cross-border related-party transactions, the remuneration method, comparability evidence, and any advance pricing arrangements or unilateral rulings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg resident person or Luxembourg PE whose SCSp has intercompany transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 in a tax year must complete Schedule 200F. Non-resident partners are not required to file solely by reason of ownership of a transparent SCSp.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing carries a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax after the first notice, rising to 30% after repeated formal notices; in fraud cases the surcharge can reach 50% to 100%. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month. Failure to file Schedule 200F or the master/local transfer pricing file can attract an administrative fine of up to EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Luxembourg resident capital company. Distributions from a transparent SCSp to its partners do not trigger Luxembourg withholding tax at the SCSp level. If an underlying Luxembourg operating company in the family-office structure pays dividends to the SCSp, the payer must withhold 15% unless a treaty or the Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces the rate to 0%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty or EU directive relief, the beneficial owner must provide the Luxembourg payer: (i) an original current tax-residence certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the state of residence; (ii) Form 22 (or the applicable ACD e-form) for reduced withholding at source or a refund of Luxembourg tax withheld; and (iii) a beneficial-ownership declaration. For EU parent companies, evidence of at least 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and a 12-month holding period is required. Because the SCSp is transparent, the TRC and beneficial-ownership declaration must be obtained for the underlying partners, not only for the SCSp itself.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax on arm's-length royalties paid to non-residents where the intellectual property is not attributable to a Luxembourg PE; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive also applies to associated EU companies. Interest: 0% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax on cross-border debt interest paid to non-resident lenders, subject to recharacterisation under anti-abuse rules or if an instrument is treated as equity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 100,000 in annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers the obligation to attach the Luxembourg Transfer Pricing Schedule (Form 200F). The full Local File is required for relevant taxpayers above the same EUR 100,000 threshold; the Master File is generally required for groups with consolidated turnover above EUR 50 million; CbC Report filings apply above EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a standalone statute; however, the ACD enforces substance requirements through the general anti-abuse rule, the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, the EU ATAD, and the doctrine of substance over form. A single-family office SCSp must have real management in Luxembourg, substantive local decisions, an office or contractual outsourcing arrangement with genuine service providers, local bank accounts, and adequate records to evidence beneficial ownership; otherwise it may be recharacterised as an opaque shell, denied treaty benefits, or regarded as a permanent establishment of the non-resident family.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately filing a false Luxembourg tax return, concealing assets held through the SCSp, falsifying partner allocations, or knowingly under-reporting a Luxembourg PE's income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 426 LIR and general criminal law: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years; criminal fine from EUR 5,000 to EUR 250,000; administrative tax increase of up to 50% to 100% of the evaded tax; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; exclusion from subsidies and public contracts in certain cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners, managing directors and tax representatives who caused or approved the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. Personal assets may be seized, directors can be subject to travel bans, and criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment, disqualification from board service, and international extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the family-office SCSp as a bare conduit without employees, office, management meetings, business records, substantive activity, or independent Luxembourg professional gatekeepers, while claiming treaty benefits or tax-transparent treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the SCSp as an opaque resident entity or as a permanent establishment of the parent family/principal; denial of treaty and EU-directive relief; reassessment of Luxembourg income and net wealth tax with penalties up to 100%; loss of the participation exemption and net-wealth tax relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is possible where the SCSp is a fictitious contract used to commit fraud or evade mandatory law. The general partner and directors may be held personally liable for company liabilities and unpaid taxes if they have knowingly allowed an abuse of the corporate form; in insolvency, directors may face clawback actions and civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to document cross-border related-party transactions in the SCSp group, applying a non-arm's-length management fee or interest rate, or refusing to provide the Luxembourg TP file upon ACD request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to the arm's-length margin; interest on underpaid tax at 0.6% per month; penalty for non-disclosure or late filing of up to EUR 250,000; loss of access to mutual agreement procedure protections where documentation is materially incomplete; risk of secondary adjustment and constructive dividend treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve a non-arm's-length price can be liable for breach of fiduciary duty to the partnership and, in the event of fraudulent pricing, for restitution of the tax deficiency. Criminal liability attaches where transfer pricing is used as a sham to conceal diversion of profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owners of the family-office assets, failure to file the Luxembourg UBO register, omission of CRS or FATCA reports, or using the SCSp to launder proceeds of tax evasion or predicate offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended): CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 2.5 million or 10% of the entity's annual turnover; penal sanctions for directors and managers up to EUR 1.25 million and imprisonment up to 5 years; deregistration or closure of the vehicle; prohibition from conducting financial-sector activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner may be personally fined, disqualified, and criminally prosecuted for money-laundering facilitation. In cases where tax evasion by the family is channeled through the SCSp, the AML conviction can trigger restitution orders, freezing orders, and travel restrictions against the responsible individuals.
